scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9104: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team is convinced their own edge router,
router1, has fallen over and want router1 restarted. Please find and confirm the
real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on router2: its BGP routing daemon (bgpd) has been killed, so
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and the inter-AS prefixes are
no longer exchanged. With no route to the peer AS, pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket MISDIRECTS to router1 (the user's own edge router),
but the fault is on the PEER side: router2 is the eBGP speaker whose daemon is
dead. router1 is healthy -- its bgpd is still running and its inter-AS interface
is up; it simply has no session because router2 stopped speaking BGP.

The correct diagnosis identifies router2 (bgpd down) as the faulty device and
explicitly EXONERATES router1: router1's BGP daemon and interfaces are fine, so
the user's "router1 has fallen over" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that restarts
/ blames router1 has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router2" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router2 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router1 re-establishes, router2 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router2 is down (the peer eBGP speaker), not a fault on router1
bonus-exonerates-router1: notes router1's bgpd is up and its inter-AS interface is healthy, rejecting the ticket's "router1 fell over" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the BGP routing process (FRRouting/bgpd) on router2 has failed. Mechanism: With BGP down on router2, no inter-AS routes are exchanged across the interconnect 193.10.11.0/24. As a result, router1 has only its directly connected networks and no route to 200.1.1.0/24. When pc1 sends traffic to pc2, router1 (195.11.14.1) returns ICMP “Destination Net Unreachable,” which matches the user’s symptom.

Localization: 
- pc1→pc2 ping fails with “From 195.11.14.1 Destination Net Unreachable.”
- router1 routing table shows only connected routes (195.11.14.0/24, 193.10.11.0/24) and no 200.1.1.0/24.
- On router1, “show ip bgp summary” displays neighbor 193.10.11.2 (AS 2) in Active (no established session), despite FRR being active.
- On router2, FRR service status is failed and “show ip bgp summary” reports “bgpd is not running.”

Root cause: The FRR/bgpd daemon on router2 is down, preventing the BGP session with router1 from establishing and withdrawing all learned routes.

Corrective fix: Restart the FRR service on router2 (systemctl restart frr), verify bgpd is running and the BGP neighbor 193.10.11.1 transitions to Established, and confirm 200.1.1.0/24 appears in router1’s RIB. Also ensure FRR is enabled to start on boot and review FRR logs/config for the reason it failed. No restart is needed on router1.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states FRRouting/bgpd on router2 is down as the root cause and exonerates router1 (no restart needed).

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-router1: notes router1's bgpd is up and its inter-AS interface is healthy, rejecting the ticket's "router1 fell over" hypothesis

Proposes restarting FRR/bgpd on router2 and verifying the BGP session and route advertisement, matching the expected remediation.
